text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said a National Housing Price Index will be introduced in a move to help curb excessive speculation in the property market.
-- Historical buildings less than a century-old, which are unprotected under existing antiquity regulations, will no longer be at the mercy of developers under new legislation being drafted.
-- The Malaysian Airlines Pilots Association should reconsider the management's revised offer of a 27 percent pay increase, Malaysia Airlines chairman Tajudin Ramli said.

-- A securities regulatory process which combines the strengths of government guidance with the benefits of self-regulation will make for the most effective and efficient overall regulatory system, Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange president Mohd Salleh Majid says.
-- Buyers will soon be able to determine how much they should pay for a house without falling prey to speculative prices following the completion of the National Housing Price Index.

-- All eyes will be on the Cabinet Committee on Social Issues as it meets today to discuss the problems affecting the young. But politicians, community leaders, NGOs and others are already pointing their fingers at parents.
